blinding.existing_candidates: not_blinded: reviewer previously inspected their old policy outputs during review
blinding.new_delivery_variants: no new policy outputs read before labeling; labels authored from task wording, not programmatic requirements comparisons

scope: Manually reasoned labels for curated fictional candidate specifications and source-linked historical summaries. No observed natural error-rate estimate. No general profile-extraction validation.
eligibility_definition: Candidate eligibility for exact buyer quote review, not purchase authorization or permission to execute payment.
delivery_variant_assumptions: All non-delivery properties and complete quote of work-resolable remain fixed.
Candidate day count is an explicit merchant commitment, not an estimate or buyer note.
Day counts are measured from the same order-date anchor.
The buyer deadline means no later than fourteen days; earlier delivery qualifies.

labels.reason: The buyer explicitly rejects substitutes for Extra Wide/EE. Merchant labels this candidate Standard; a matching size and a total below $150 do not cure the explicit width conflict.

Within the buyer-confirmed test-merchant adaptation, one size 10.5 pair explicitly labeled Extra Wide matches the stated width and size; $114.94 complete test quote is below $150. This is eligibility for buyer quote review, not approval to spend. Letter-code equivalence is not generalized across brands.

The buyer expressly requires shoes that can be resoled. Candidate evidence leaves this property unknown. Other matching specifications and a $210.34 total are insufficient to approve review as fully compliant; unknown is not proof that the shoe cannot be resoled.

The test merchant explicitly documents resoling, black leather lace-up style, size 11 Wide, availability and 14-day delivery. For the controlled assumption that delivery days are a merchant commitment measured from the same order date, it meets the two-week deadline. The $210.34 complete quote is below $250. Actual purchase still needs exact approval.
A documented commitment to arrive within seven days satisfies a deadline of two weeks; earlier arrival is not a mismatch. All other candidate evidence is held fixed and compliant.
A documented commitment to arrive within fourteen days meets the two-week deadline at its boundary, assuming a common order-date anchor and no additional qualification. Other facts are held fixed.
A commitment to deliver only within fifteen days does not meet the explicit two-week deadline. Other compliant properties do not override the deadline.
Without a merchant arrival commitment, the two-week deadline cannot be verified. This is an evidence gap, not demonstrated lateness. Other properties are held fixed.

public_release_scope: Only eight controlled labels with shipped source pointers are included. Historical-summary reviews remain outside this public release and its evaluation denominators.
